summary: Two maturity levels that must not be blurred. Where keys live the vault is draft M2 packages/ai design only not shipping; BYOK with no Vaudeville-operated inference; non-secret vault.json metadata apart from secret material in OS keychain or AES-256-GCM file; never logged never in export; open binding and CI questions remain. The loopback server is shipping: binds 127.0.0.1 only, entity scripts never evaluated server-side; per-launch bearer in vaude-session meta never logged or persisted never handed to sandbox; api gate checkApiRequest fails closed before bind, Host DNS-rebinding defense, GET HEAD no token but refuse Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, POST demands Origin and timingSafeEqual token; gate does not reject loopback aliases and is weaker on reads; body caps 64MB inspect 32MB JSON fail closed. Sandbox origin shipping code with packaged proof BLOCKED: second loopback allowlist only worker wasm, CORS to UI origin, no token; proven at Bun HTTP layer not measured in WebView2; do not claim full isolation; same-origin fallback degraded.

sections.title: Where keys live (the vault, spec only)
sections.summary: Draft vault only: key-vault.md status draft milestone M2 package packages/ai which does not exist yet; future-tense design not running code. BYOK per ADR-006: user supplies Anthropic OpenRouter OpenAI Gemini or OpenAI-compatible credentials with no Vaudeville-operated inference account or proxy. Vault is packages/ai zero UI consumed by CLI and agent loop never on a server. Two kinds of state kept apart: non-secret metadata in vault.json versus secret material only in backends. Two backends chosen at first use: OS keychain when canary succeeds else encrypted file vault.key plus vault.enc AES-256-GCM with DECRYPT_FAILED refuse never silent regenerate. Never logged is a hard invariant; never in an export because keys are outside the entity graph. Not yet decided covers binding single-exe CI env override and size limits.

children.title: Two kinds of state, kept apart
children.summary: Only one half is ever secret. Non-secret metadata in ~/.hoplight/vault.json holds provider kind label base URL organization id and names of extra headers never values that could carry a token; plain JSON safe to read. Secret material is the API key string plus any extraHeaders values which can carry a bearer, keyed by provider config id, only in one of the two backends never in vault.json. Types enforce the split: ProviderConfig safe versus ProviderSecret apiKey and optional extraHeaders never logged; only getApiKey plus backend internals hold a ProviderSecret.

children.title: Two backends, chosen at first use
children.summary: First use probes OS keychain and records the choice. OS keychain Windows Credential Manager macOS Keychain Linux Secret Service when a native binding loads and a canary write-then-read succeeds; one entry per config service hoplight account providerConfig.id secret JSON of apiKey and optional extraHeaders. Encrypted file elsewhere with one-time stderr warning: vault.key 32 bytes crypto.randomBytes once chmod 600 or Windows ACL is the local secret not a passphrase not KDF-stretched; vault.enc AES-256-GCM fresh 96-bit IV per write auth tag appended atomic temp fsync rename. Corrupted vault.enc fails GCM auth; vault must refuse load with DECRYPT_FAILED never silently regenerate a key or proceed with an empty vault.

children.title: Never logged
children.summary: Hard invariant because vault consumers include the agent loop whose traces users paste into bug reports. Exactly three functions return raw key material: getApiKey getSecret and resolveRole. Every other read path omits apiKey and extraHeaders values entirely not masked with a partial suffix because a masked suffix is still key material. Shared redactSecrets deep-strips key-shaped fields at the agent spill store boundary rather than trusted to each caller. VaultError carries providerConfigId and label never the key even on DECRYPT_FAILED. CLI reads through hidden non-echoing input and never prints it back including in --json output.

children.title: Never in an export
children.summary: The vault is structurally outside the export path, stronger than a scrub pass. It is a packages/ai component for CLI and agent loop; the UI export route operates on canonical entities and a canonical entity has no key field. Keys are not filtered out at export time; they were never in the entity graph an export walks. redactSecrets guards the agent loop spill store, a different boundary.

children.title: Not yet decided
children.summary: Open questions from the draft spec unresolved at writing. Which native keychain binding ships and whether a native .node addon loads inside bun build --compile single-executable; the fallback-to-file path must work regardless. Whether an environment-variable key override for CI is supported in v1. Per-platform keychain size limits and whether an oversize secret forces file mode.

sections.title: The loopback server (shipping)
sections.summary: Shipping code with automated Bun tests. Visual app binds Bun.serve hostname 127.0.0.1 only; thin shell over the same engine as CLI; nothing in an uploaded entity is evaluated server-side and scripts inside cards are data. Per-launch bearer is randomBytes base64url never log or persist, injected as escaped meta vaude-session for trusted apiFetch, never handed to the sandbox origin. The api gate checkApiRequest runs before every api handler; static assets ungated. Gate order: fail closed 503 if Host Origin or token unset; Host every method for DNS-rebinding; GET HEAD no token but refuse Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site; POST demands loopback Origin fail closed on null and timingSafeEqual token; other methods 405. What the gate does not do: accepts localhost and ::1 on correct port; GET HEAD not token-gated so header-less clients pass reads. Body caps INSPECT 64MB JSON 32MB with early Content-Length and running total.

children.title: The per-launch bearer
children.summary: A fresh bearer is minted once per launch as randomBytes(32).toString base64url in createSecurityContext marked never log or persist. injectSessionMeta puts it into served HTML as an escaped meta name vaude-session which the trusted UI reads to authenticate its own API calls. The token stays in that meta tag and the trusted apiFetch path; it is never handed to the sandbox origin.

children.title: The /api/* gate
children.summary: Every api route runs through checkApiRequest before any handler; static assets serve ungated because they are not secret. Order: if expected Host Origin or token is not yet filled return 503 fail closed before bind. Host on every method: hostAllowed exact host port or loopback-equivalent spelling 127.0.0.1 localhost ::1 on the same port else 403; DNS-rebinding defense against attacker hostnames resolved to loopback. GET and HEAD carry no token; they are refused only when Sec-Fetch-Site is cross-site a browser-set header a page cannot forge so img loads cannot be a blind existence oracle if token were required. POST demands Origin loopback-equivalent and null Origin fails closed; token compared with crypto.timingSafeEqual and zero-length compares false. Any other method returns 405.

children.title: What the gate does not do
children.summary: Stated plainly because overclaiming would be a defect. localhost and ::1 on the correct port are accepted not rejected; only wrong port or foreign hostname fails closed. All three loopback spellings resolve to the same bound interface so rejecting localhost would paper-cut bookmarks while protecting nothing; the gate stops attacker hostnames not loopback aliases. GET and HEAD are not token-gated: a header-less client curl or older browser with no Sec-Fetch-Site passes the read gate. The read gate is deliberately weaker than the mutation gate. Reads that expose entity data rely on the loopback bind and cross-site refusal not on the bearer.

children.title: Body caps
children.summary: Request bodies stream with a hard byte cap and 413 on overflow: INSPECT_BODY_MAX 64MB JSON_BODY_MAX 32MB. readBodyCapped checks Content-Length early when present and enforces a running total as it reads so a lying or absent length header still cannot exceed the cap. Same fail-closed posture the upload adapters use against zip bombs.

sections.title: The sandbox origin (shipping code, packaged proof BLOCKED)
sections.summary: Untrusted Lua from the Risu Test Bench runs in a Worker from a second loopback listener on an ephemeral port, a distinct origin from UI and api. Defense-in-depth: same-origin Worker is a killable thread not an origin boundary so a future WebView or bundler bug would widen blast radius if same-origin. Fails closed by construction: serves only sandbox worker.js regex-worker.js and glue.wasm; every other path 404 with locked CSP; no api no index HTML no session token no traversal. CORS limited to exact UI origin plus loopback aliases so only trusted UI constructs the cross-origin module Worker. API token is never injected into anything this host serves. What is proven and what is not: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence proven at Bun HTTP layer; packaged WebView2 isolation not measured; Plan 017 BLOCKED; do not claim fully isolated; same-origin fallback degraded not claimed isolated.

children.title: What is proven, and what is not
children.summary: Scaffolding additive to token Plan 005 and resource quotas Plan 016 not a replacement. Proven: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence by Bun HTTP and handler tests. Not measured: packaged WebView2 origin isolation, whether WebView collapses two loopback authorities, crossOriginIsolated and storage separation, and credentialed API fetch from sandbox origin; Plan 017 BLOCKED until a WebView2 smoke matrix records those. Do not call the sandbox fully isolated sandboxed or exploit-proof. Until the matrix is green it is defense-in-depth with tested HTTP behavior and unmeasured in-WebView separation. Sandbox bind failure falls back to same-origin Worker explicitly degraded and not claimed isolated.
